classification.difficultyReason: Infer the rectangle's width from the semicircle radius, then subtract two semicircle areas.

content.prompt: Two semicircles, each of radius $3\text{ cm}$, are cut from a rectangle of length $12\text{ cm}$, as shown below.

spec.description: Two upward semicircles lie side by side inside a rectangle. Their diameters partition its bottom edge and their arcs touch its top edge. Each centre is marked, and each left half-diameter is labelled 3 cm. House style replaces ordinary blue outlines and red centre markers with black; no shading is added.
spec.mathematics: Each semicircle has radius 3 cm and diameter 6 cm. The rectangle spans two diameters horizontally and one radius vertically. The 12 cm length remains in the stem only.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear; the rectangle width and remaining area are not labelled.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the width of the rectangle?

answer.worked: The width is the perpendicular distance from a semicircle's diameter to the top of its arc, which equals its radius. Therefore, the width is $3\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What is the area remaining? Leave your answer in terms of $\pi$.

answer.short:
$(36-9\pi)\text{ cm}^2$

Subtract the combined area of the two semicircles from the rectangle's area.
answer.worked:
The two semicircles together have the area of one circle of radius $3\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{rectangle}}&=12\times3\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=36\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{two semicircles}}&=2\times\frac12\times\pi\times3^2\\A_{\text{two semicircles}}&=9\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{remaining}}&=A_{\text{rectangle}}-A_{\text{two semicircles}}\\A_{\text{remaining}}&=(36-9\pi)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
